blocks.en: The Raid
blocks.zh: 突袭

blocks.en: Early in April of 1958, my wife and I arrived, malarial and diffident, in a Balinese village we intended, as anthropologists, to study. A small place, about five hundred people, and relatively remote, it was its own world. We were intruders, professional ones, and the villagers dealt with us as Balinese seem always to deal with people not part of their life who yet press themselves upon them: as though we were not there. For them, and to a degree for ourselves, we were nonpersons, specters, invisible men.
blocks.zh: 1958 年 4 月初，我和妻子带着疟疾和羞怯来到巴厘岛的一个村庄，我们打算作为人类学家进行研究。地方不大，五百人左右，又比较偏僻，却是一片自己的天地。我们是入侵者，是专业人士，村民们对待我们就像巴厘人对待我们一样，似乎总是对待那些不属于他们生活的人，但他们却向他们施加压力：就好像我们不在那里一样。对于他们来说，在某种程度上对于我们自己来说，我们都是非人、幽灵、隐形人。

blocks.en: We moved into an extended family compound (that had been arranged before through the provincial government) belonging to one of the four major factions in village life. But except for our landlord and the village chief, whose cousin and brother-in-law he was, everyone ignored us in a way only a Balinese can do. As we wandered around, uncertain, wistful, eager to please, people seemed to look right through us with a gaze focused several yards behind us on some more actual stone or tree. Almost nobody almost as satisfactory. If we ventured to approach someone (something one is powerfully inhibited from doing in such an atmosphere), he moved, negligently but definitively, away. If, seated or leaning against a wall, we had him trapped, he said nothing at all, or mumbled what for the Balinese is the ultimate nonword-"yes." The indifference, of course, was studied; the villagers were watching every move we made and they had an enormous amount of quite accurate information about who we were and what we were going to be doing. But they acted as if we simply did not exist, which, in fact, as this behavior was designed to inform us, we did not, or anyway not yet.
blocks.zh: 我们搬进了一个大家庭大院（之前是通过省政府安排的），属于乡村生活的四大派系之一。但除了我们的房东和村长（他是他们的表弟和妹夫）之外，每个人都忽视我们，只有巴厘人才能做到这一点。当我们四处闲逛时，不确定、渴望、渴望取悦，人们似乎在看穿我们，目光聚焦在我们身后几码远的一些更真实的石头或树上。几乎没有人令人满意。如果我们冒险接近某人（在这种气氛下，人们会强烈禁止这样做），他就会疏忽但明确地走开。如果他坐着或靠在墙上，我们把他困住了，他什么也不说，或者咕哝着，对巴厘人来说，这是终极的非字眼——“是”。当然，这种冷漠是经过研究的。村民们注视着我们的一举一动，他们掌握了大量关于我们是谁以及我们要做什么的非常准确的信息。但他们的表现就好像我们根本不存在一样，事实上，这种行为的目的是告诉我们，我们不存在，或者无论如何还不存在。

blocks.en: My wife and I were still very much in the gust of wind stage, a most frustrating, and even, as you soon begin to doubt whether you are really real after all, unnerving one, when, ten days or so after our arrival, a large cockfight was held in the public square to raise money for a new school.
blocks.zh: 我和我的妻子还处于一阵风的阶段，这是一个最令人沮丧的阶段，甚至，当你很快开始怀疑自己是否真的真实时，甚至令人不安，在我们到达十天左右的时候，在公共广场上举行了一场大型斗鸡活动，为一所新学校筹集资金。

blocks.en: Now, a few special occasions aside, cockfights are illegal in Bali under the Republic (as, for not altogether unrelated reasons, they were under the Dutch), largely as a result of the pretensions to puritanism radical nationalism tends to bring with it. The elite, which is not itself so very puritan, worries about the poor, ignorant peasant gambling all his money away, about what cockfighting as "primitive," "backward," "unprogressive," and generally unbecoming an ambitious nation. And, as with those other embarrassments -opium smoking, begging, or uncovered breasts-it seeks, rather unsystematically, to put a stop to it.
blocks.zh: 现在，除了一些特殊场合之外，斗鸡在共和国统治下的巴厘岛是非法的（因为并非完全不相关的原因，斗鸡在荷兰统治下），很大程度上是由于激进民族主义往往会带来清教主义的结果​​。精英阶层本身并不是那么清教徒，他们担心贫穷、无知的农民把所有的钱都赌光了，担心斗鸡是“原始的”、“落后的”、“不进步的”，而且通常不适合一个雄心勃勃的国家。而且，就像其他令人尴尬的事情——吸鸦片、乞讨或裸露乳房一样——它试图相当不系统地制止这种现象。

blocks.en: As a result, the fights are usually held in a secluded corner of a village in semisecrecy, a fact which tends to slow the action a little-not very much, but the Balinese do not care to have it slowed at all. In this case, however, perhaps because they were raising money for a school that the government was unable to give them, perhaps because raids had been few recently, perhaps, as I gathered from subsequent discussion, there was a notion that the necessary bribes had been paid, they thought they could take a chance on the central square and draw a larger and more enthusiastic crowd without attracting the attention of the law.
blocks.zh: 因此，战斗通常在村庄的一个僻静角落半秘密地进行，这一事实往往会稍微放慢行动速度，但巴厘人根本不介意放慢速度。然而，在这种情况下，也许是因为他们正在为一所政府无法提供给他们的学校筹集资金，也许是因为最近袭击很少，也许，正如我从随后的讨论中了解到的那样，有一种观念认为，必要的贿赂已经支付了，他们认为他们可以在中心广场上碰碰运气，吸引更多、更热情的人群，而不引起法律的注意。

blocks.en: They were wrong. In the midst of the third match, with hundreds of people, including, still transparent, myself and my wife, fused into a single body around the ring, a superorganism in the literal sense, a truck full of policemen armed with machine guns roared up. Amid great screeching cries of "pulisi! pulisi!" from the crowd, the policemen jumped out, and, springing into the center of the ring, began to swing their guns around like gangsters in a motion picture, though not going so far as actually to fire them. The superorganism came instantly apart as its components scattered in all directions. People raced down the road, disappeared head first over walls, scrambled under platforms, folded sharp enough to cut off a finger or run a hole through a foot were running wildly around. Everything was dust and panic.
blocks.zh: 他们错了。在第三场比赛进行到一半的时候，数百人，包括仍然透明的我和我的妻子，在擂台周围融合成一个整体，一个字面意义上的超级有机体，一辆满载手持机关枪的警察的卡车呼啸而来。在“普力斯！普力斯！”的尖叫声中。警察从人群中跳了出来，跳到了围场中央，开始像电影里的歹徒一样挥舞着枪，但并没有真正开枪。超级有机体瞬间分崩离析，其组成部分向四面八方散开。人们沿着道路奔跑，头朝下消失在墙壁上，在平台下爬行，折叠得锋利得足以割断手指或在脚上穿出一个洞，人们疯狂地四处奔跑。一切都是灰尘和恐慌。

blocks.en: On the established anthropological principle, When in Rome, my wife and I decided, only slightly less instantaneously than everyone else, that the thing to do was run too. We ran down the main village street, northward, away from where we were living, for we were on that side of the ring. About half-way down another fugitive ducked suddenly into a compound-his own, it turned out-and we, seeing nothing ahead of us but rice fields, open country, and a very high volcano, followed him. As the three of us came tumbling into the courtyard, his wife, who had apparently been through this sort of thing before, whipped out a table, a tablecloth, three chairs, and three cups of tea, and we all, without any explicit communication whatsoever, sat down, commenced to sip tea, and sought to compose ourselves.
blocks.zh: 根据既定的人类学原则，在罗马时，我和我的妻子决定，要做的事情也是跑步，只是比其他人稍微慢一点。我们沿着村庄的主要街道向北跑，远离我们住的地方，因为我们在环的那一侧。大约走到一半的时候，另一个逃亡者突然躲进一处院落——原来是他自己的院落——而我们，除了稻田、开阔的田野和一座很高的火山之外，什么也看不见，就跟在他后面。当我们三人跌跌撞撞地走进院子时，他的妻子显然以前经历过这种事情，拿出一张桌子、一块桌布、三把椅子和三杯茶，我们大家在没有任何明确的交流的情况下坐下来，开始喝茶，试图让自己平静下来。

blocks.en: A few moments later, one of the policemen marched importantly into the yard, looking for the village chief. (The chief had not only been at the fight, he had arranged it. When the truck drove up he ran to the river, stripped off his sarong, and plunged in so he could say, when at length they found him sitting there pouring water over his head, that he had been away bathing when the whole affair had occurred and was ignorant of it. They did not believe him and fined him three hundred rupiah, which the village raised collectively.) Seeing my wife and I, "White Men," there in the yard, the policeman performed a classic double take. When he found his voice again he asked, approximately, what in the devil did we think we were doing there. Our host of five minutes leaped instantly to our defense, producing an impassioned description of who and what we were, so detailed and so accurate that it was my turn, having barely communicated with a living human being save my landlord and the village chief for more than a week, to be astonished. We had a perfect right to be there, he said, looking the Javanese upstart in the eye. We were American professors; the government had cleared us; we were there to study culture; we were going to write a book to tell Americans about Bali. And we had all been there drinking tea and talking about cultural matters all afternoon and did not know anything about any cockfight. Moreover, we had not seen the village chief all day, he must have gone to town. The policeman retreated in rather total disarray. And, after a decent interval, bewildered but relieved to have survived and stayed out of jail, so did we.
blocks.zh: 过了一会儿，一名警察神气十足地走进院子，寻找村长。 （酋长不仅参加了战斗，而且还安排了这场战斗。当卡车开到河边时，他跑到河边，脱掉纱笼，跳进水里，以便他可以说，当最后他们发现他坐在那里，把水倒在头上时，他在整个事件发生时正在外面洗澡，对此一无所知。他们不相信他，并罚款他三百卢比，这是村里集体筹集的。）在那里看到我和我的妻子和我，“白人”，在那里在院子里，警察做了一个经典的双重观察。当他再次找到自己的声音时，他大致问道，我们到底以为我们在那里做什么。五分钟的主持人立刻站出来为我们辩护，对我们是谁、是什么进行了热情洋溢的描述，如此详细、如此准确，轮到我了，我在一个多星期的时间里几乎没有与除了房东和村长之外的活人交流过，我感到惊讶不已。我们完全有权利去那里，他看着这位爪哇新贵的眼睛说道。我们是美国教授；政府已经批准了我们；我们去那里是为了学习文化；我们打算写一本书来向美国人介绍巴厘岛。我们整个下午都在那里喝茶、谈论文化问题，对斗鸡一无所知。而且，我们一整天都没有见到村长，他一定是进城了。警察狼狈地撤退了。经过一段相当长的一段时间后，我们感到困惑，但又庆幸自己幸存下来并没有出狱，我们也是如此。

blocks.en: The next morning the village was a completely different world for us. Not only were we no longer invisible, we were suddenly the center of all attention, the object of a great outpouring of warmth, interest, and, most especially, amusement. Everyone in the village knew we had fled like everyone else. They asked us about it again and again (I must have told the story, small detail by small detail, fifty times by the end of the day), gently, affectionately, but quite insistently teasing us: "Why didn't you just stand there and tell the police who you were?" "Why didn't you just say you were only watching and not betting?" "Were you really afraid of those little guns?" As always, kinesthetically minded and, even when fleeing for their lives (or, as happened eight years later, surrendering them), the world's most poised people, they gleefully mimicked, also over and over again, our graceless style of running and what they claimed were our panic-stricken facial expressions. But above all, everyone was extremely pleased and even more surprised that we had not simply "pulled out our papers" (they knew about those too) and asserted our Distinguished Visitor status, but had instead demonstrated our solidarity with what were now our covillagers. (What we had actually demonstrated was our cowardice, but there is fellowship in that too.) Even the Brahmana priest, an old, grave, halfway-to-Heaven type who because of its associations with the underworld would never be involved, even distantly, in a cockfight, and was difficult to approach even to other Balinese, had us called into his courtyard to ask us about what had happened, chuckling happily at the sheer extraordinariness of it all.
blocks.zh: 第二天早上，这个村庄对我们来说是一个完全不同的世界。我们不仅不再是隐形的，而且突然成为所有人关注的中心，成为热情、兴趣、尤其是娱乐的对象。村里的每个人都知道我们和其他人一样逃走了。他们一次又一次地问我们这个问题（我肯定已经把这个故事一个个细节一个个细节地讲了，到一天结束时已经讲了五十遍了），温柔地、亲切地，但相当坚持地取笑我们：“你为什么不站在那里告诉警察你是谁？” “你为什么不直接说你只是看，不是赌？” “你真的害怕那些小枪吗？”一如既往，他们充满动觉，即使在逃命时（或者，八年后，他们投降了），他们是世界上最泰然自若的人，他们兴高采烈地模仿着我们粗鲁的奔跑风格，以及他们声称的我们惊慌失措的面部表情。但最重要的是，每个人都非常高兴，甚至更惊讶的是，我们不是简单地“拿出我们的文件”（他们也知道这些）并声称我们的尊贵访客身份，而是表明了我们与现在我们的村民的团结。 （我们实际上表现出的是我们的怯懦，但也有团契。）即使是婆罗门祭司，一个古老、严肃、半途而废的人，因为与地狱有联系，永远不会参与斗鸡，即使是遥远的，即使是其他巴厘人也很难接近，他也把我们叫到他的院子里，问我们发生了什么事，并为这一切的非凡而高兴地咯咯笑。

blocks.en: In Bali, to be teased is to be accepted. It was the turning point so far as our relationship to the community was concerned, and we were quite literally "in." The whole village opened up to us, probably more than it ever would have otherwise (I might actually never have gotten to that priest and our accidental host became one of my best informants), and certainly very much faster. Getting caught, or almost caught, in a vice raid is perhaps not a very generalizable recipe for achieving that mysterious necessity of anthropological field work, rapport, but for me it worked very well. It led to a sudden and unusually complete acceptance into a society extremely difficult for outsiders to penetrate. It gave me the kind of immediate, inside view grasp of an aspect of "peasant mentality" that anthropologists not fortunate enough to flee headlong with their subjects from armed authorities normally do not get. And, perhaps most important of all, for the other things might have come in other ways, it put me very quickly on to a combination emotional explosion, status war, and philosophical drama of central significance to the society whose inner nature I desired to understand. By the time I left I had spent about as much time looking into cockfights as into witchcraft, irrigation, caste, or marriage.
blocks.zh: 在巴厘岛，被嘲笑就是被接受。就我们与社区的关系而言，这是一个转折点，我们确实“融入”了。整个村庄向我们敞开心扉，可能比以往任何时候都更加开放（我实际上可能永远不会接触到那个牧师，而我们偶然的主人成为我最好的线人之一），而且当然要快得多。对于实现人类学田野工作的神秘必要性——融洽关系来说，在一次恶行袭击中被抓，或者几乎被抓，也许不是一个非常普遍的方法，但对我来说，它非常有效。它导致人们突然异常完全地接受了一个外人极难渗透的社会。它让我对“农民心态”的一个方面有一种直接的、内部的了解，而那些不幸带着他们的研究对象逃离武装当局的人类学家通常无法得到这种了解。也许最重要的是，因为其他事情可能以其他方式出现，它很快让我陷入了情感爆发、地位之争和对我渴望了解其内在本质的社会具有核心意义的哲学戏剧的结合。当我离开时，我花在研究斗鸡上的时间与研究巫术、灌溉、种姓或婚姻的时间差不多。

blocks.en: Of Cocks and Men
blocks.zh: 公鸡和男人

blocks.en: As much of America surfaces in a ball park, on a golf links, at a race track, or around a poker table, much of Bali surfaces in a cock ring. For it is only apparently cocks that are fighting there. Actually, it is men.
blocks.zh: 美国的大部分地区都是在棒球场、高尔夫球场、赛马场或扑克桌上，而巴厘岛的大部分地区都是在斗鸡场。因为显然只是公鸡在那里打架。其实，是男人。

blocks.en: To anyone who has been in Bali any length of time, the deep psychological identification of Balinese men with their cocks is unmistakable. The double entendre here is deliberate. It works in exactly the same way in Balinese as it does in English, even to producing the same tired jokes, strained puns, and uninventive obscenities. Bateson and Mead have even suggested that, in line with the Balinese conception of the body as a set of separately animated parts, cocks are viewed as detachable, self-operating penises, ambulant genitals with a life of their own. And while I do not have the kind of unconscious material either to confirm or disconfirm this intriguing notion, the fact that they are masculine symbols par excellence is about as indubitable, and to the Balinese about as evident, as the fact that water runs downhill.
blocks.zh: 对于任何在巴厘岛呆过一段时间的人来说，巴厘岛男人对阴茎的深刻心理认同是显而易见的。这里的双关语是故意的。它在巴厘岛语中的运作方式与在英语中的运作方式完全相同，甚至会产生同样的乏味笑话、紧张的双关语和毫无创意的猥亵内容。贝特森和米德甚至提出，根据巴厘人将身体视为一组独立的活动部分的概念，公鸡被视为可拆卸的、自我操作的阴茎、具有自己生命的移动性生殖器。虽然我没有那种无意识的材料来证实或反驳这个有趣的概念，但它们是卓越的男性象征这一事实是不容置疑的，对于巴厘人来说，就像水往低处流的事实一样明显。

blocks.en: The language of everyday moralism is shot through, on the male side of it, with roosterish imagery. Sabung, the word for cock (and one which appears in inscriptions as early as A.D. 922 ), is used metaphorically to mean "hero," "warrior," "champion," "man of parts," "political candidate," "bachelor," "dandy," "lady-killer," or "tough guy." A pompous man whose behavior presumes above his station is compared to a tailless cock who struts about as though he had a large, spectacular one. A desperate man who makes a last, irrational effort to extricate himself from an impossible situation is likened to a dying cock who makes one final lunge at his tormentor to drag him along to a common destruction. A stingy man, who promises much, gives little, and begrudges that is compared to a cock which, held by the tail, leaps at another without in fact engaging him. A marriageable young man still shy with the opposite sex or someone in a new job anxious to make a good impression is called "a fighting cock caged for the first time." Court trials, wars, political contests, inheritance disputes, and street arguments are all compared to cockfights. Even the very island itself is perceived from its shape as a small, proud cock, poised, neck extended, back taut, tail raised, in eternal challenge to large, feckless, shapeless Java.
blocks.zh: 日常道德主义的语言在男性方面充满了公鸡的意象。 Sabung 是“公鸡”一词（早在公元 922 年就出现在铭文中），被用来比喻“英雄”、“战士”、“冠军”、“男人”、“政治候选人”、“单身汉”、“花花公子”、“女士杀手”或“硬汉”。一个举止高高在上的自以为是的人就像一只无尾的公鸡，趾高气扬地走来走去，好像他有一只巨大而壮观的公鸡。一个绝望的人做出最后的、非理性的努力来摆脱不可能的处境，就像一只垂死的公鸡向他的折磨者做出最后的冲刺，将他拖向共同的毁灭。一个吝啬的人，许诺多，付出少，而且吝惜，这就像一只公鸡，抓住尾巴，向另一只鸡扑去，实际上却没有与他接触。即将结婚的年轻人对异性仍然害羞，或者刚参加新工作而急于给人留下好印象，这被称为“第一次关笼的斗鸡”。法庭审判、战争、政治较量、遗产纠纷、街头争吵都被比作斗鸡。就连这座岛屿本身，从它的形状来看，也像是一只骄傲的小公鸡，泰然自若，脖子伸长，背部绷紧，尾巴翘起，永远挑战着巨大、无能、不成形的爪哇岛。

blocks.en: But the intimacy of men with their cocks is more than metaphorical. Balinese men, or anyway a large majority of Balinese men, spend an enormous amount of time with their favorites, grooming them, feeding them, discussing them, trying them out against one another, or just gazing at them with a mixture of rapt admiration and dreamy self-absorption. Whenever you see a group of Balinese men squatting idly in the council shed or along the road in their hips down, shoulders forward, knees up fashion, half or more of them will have a rooster in his hands, holding it between his thighs, bouncing it gently up and down to strengthen its legs, ruffling its feathers with abstract sensuality, pushing it out against a neighbor's rooster to rouse its spirit, withdrawing it toward his loins to calm it again Now and then, to get a feel for another bird, a man will fiddle this way with someone else's cock for a while, but usually by moving around to than just having it passed across to him as though it were merely an

blocks.en: In the houseyard, the high-walled enclosures where the people live, fighting cocks are kept in wicker cages, moved frequently about so as to maintain the optimum balance of sun and shade. They are fed a special diet, which varies somewhat according to individual theories but which is mostly maize, sifted for impurities with far more care than it is when mere humans are going to eat it and offered to the animal kernel by kernel. Red pepper is stuffed down their beaks and up their anuses to give them spirit. They are bathed in the same ceremonial preparation of tepid water, medicinal herbs, flowers, and onions in which infants are bathed, and for a prize cock just about as often. Their combs are cropped, their plumage dressed, their spurs trimmed, their legs massaged, and they are inspected for flaws with the squinted concentration of a diamond merchant. A man who has a passion for cocks, an enthusiast in the literal sense of the term, can spend most of his life with them, and even those, the overwhelming majority, whose passion though intense has not entirely run away with them, can and do spend what seems not only to an outsider, but also to themselves an inordinate amount of time with them. "I am cock crazy," my landlord, a quite ordinary aficionado by Balinese standards, used to moan as he went to move another cage, give another bath, or conduct another feeding. "We're all cock crazy."
blocks.zh: 在人们居住的院子里，斗鸡被关在柳条笼子里，经常移动，以保持阳光和阴影的最佳平衡。它们被喂食一种特殊的饮食，根据个人的理论有所不同，但主要是玉米，比人类吃玉米时更加仔细地筛选杂质，然后将其逐粒提供给动物。红辣椒被塞进它们的喙和肛门，以给它们带来精神。他们沐浴在与婴儿沐浴相同的仪式准备中，包括温水、药草、鲜花和洋葱，对于获奖公鸡来说，沐浴的频率也差不多。他们的鸡冠被剪掉，他们的羽毛被修剪，他们的马刺被修剪，他们的腿被按摩，他们像钻石商人一样眯着眼睛专注地检查是否有瑕疵。一个对鸡巴充满热情的人，字面意义上的狂热者，可以与它们一起度过一生的大部分时间，甚至那些虽然热情强烈但并未完全消失的绝大多数人，可以而且确实花费了不仅在外人看来，而且在他们自己看来，与它们在一起的过多时间。 “我是个公鸡狂人”，我的房东，按照巴厘岛的标准，是一个相当普通的公鸡爱好者，在去搬另一个笼子、再洗一次澡或再一次喂食时常常抱怨道。 “我们都疯了。”

blocks.en: The madness has some less visible dimensions, however, because although it is true that cocks are symbolic expressions or magnifications of their owner's self, the narcissistic male ego writ out in Aesopian terms, they are also expressionsand rather more immediate ones-of what the Balinese regard as the direct inversion, aesthetically, morally, and animality.
blocks.zh: 然而，这种疯狂还有一些不那么明显的维度，因为虽然公鸡确实是主人自我的象征性表达或放大，用伊索的术语写出自恋的男性自我，但它们也是表达，而且是更直接的表达，巴厘人认为这是审美、道德和动物性的直接倒置。

blocks.en: The Balinese revulsion against any behavior as animal-like can hardly be overstressed. Babies are not allowed to crawl for that reason. Incest, though hardly approved, is a much less horrifying crime than bestiality. (The appropriate punishment for the second is death by drowning, for the first being forced to live like an animal.) Most demons are represented-in sculpture, dance, ritual, myth-in some real or fantastic animal form. The main puberty rite consists in filing the child's teeth so they will not look like animal fangs. Not only defecation but eating is regarded as a disgusting, almost obscene activity, to be conducted hurriedly and privately, because of its association with animality. Even falling down or any form of clumsiness is considered to be bad for these reasons. Aside from cocks and a few domestic animals-oxen, ducks-of no emotional significance, the Balinese are aversive to animals and treat their large number of dogs not merely callously but with a phobic cruelty. In identifying with his cock, the Balinese man is identifying not just with his ideal self, or even his penis, but also, and at the same time, with what he most fears, hates, and ambivalence being what it is, is fascinated by-The Powers of Darkness.
blocks.zh: 巴厘人对任何类似动物的行为都感到厌恶，这一点怎么强调都不为过。因此，不允许婴儿爬行。乱伦虽然很难得到认可，但远没有兽交那么可怕。 （对第二种人的适当惩罚是淹死，对第一种人则被迫像动物一样生活。） 大多数恶魔都以某种真实或奇幻的动物形式出现在雕塑、舞蹈、仪式、神话中。主要的青春期仪式包括锉掉孩子的牙齿，这样它们就不会看起来像动物的尖牙。不仅排便，连吃饭都被视为令人厌恶、近乎淫秽的活动，必须匆忙且私下进行，因为它与动物性有关。由于这些原因，即使跌倒或任何形式的笨拙也被认为是不好的。除了公鸡和一些没有情感意义的家畜（牛、鸭）外，巴厘人厌恶动物，对待他们的大量狗不仅冷酷无情，而且表现出令人恐惧的残忍态度。在认同他的阴茎时，巴厘岛男人不仅认同他理想的自我，甚至他的阴茎，而且同时也认同他最害怕、最讨厌和最矛盾的东西，最着迷的是黑暗的力量。

blocks.en: In the cockfight, man and beast, good and evil, ego and id, the creative power of aroused masculinity and the destructive power of loosened animality fuse in a bloody drama of hatred, cruelty, violence, and death. It is little wonder that when, as is the invariable rule, the owner of the winning cock takes the carcass of the loser- often torn limb from limb by its enraged owner-home to eat, he does so with a mixture of social embarrassment, moral satisfaction, aesthetic disgust, and cannibal joy.

blocks.en: The Fight
blocks.zh: 战斗

blocks.en: Cockfights (tetadjen; sabungan ) are held in a ring about fifty feet square. Usually they begin toward late afternoon and run three or four hours until sunset. About nine or ten program. Each match is precisely like the others in general pattern: there is no main match, no connection between individual matches, no variation in their completely ad hoc basis. After a fight has ended and the emotional debris is cleaned away-the bets paid, possessed- seven, eight, perhaps even a dozen men slip negligently into the ring with a cock and seek to find there a logical opponent for it. This process, which rarely takes less deal longer, is conducted in a very subdued, oblique, even dissembling manner Those not immediately involved give it at best but disguised, sidelong attention; those who, embarrassedly, are, attempt to pretend somehow that the whole thing is not really happening.
blocks.zh: 斗鸡（tetadjen；sabungan）在大约五十平方英尺的场地内举行。通常他们从下午晚些时候开始，运行三到四个小时直到日落。大约有九个或十个节目。每场比赛在一般模式上都与其他比赛完全相同：没有主要比赛，各个比赛之间没有联系，完全临时的基础上没有变化。一场战斗结束后，情感碎片被清理干净——赌注已付，拥有——七个、八个、甚至十几个人带着一只公鸡漫不经心地溜进拳击场，试图在那里找到一个合乎逻辑的对手。这个过程很少需要更长的时间，是以一种非常柔和、间接、甚至掩饰的方式进行的。那些没有立即参与的人充其量只是伪装的、旁观的关注；那些尴尬的人试图以某种方式假装整件事并没有真正发生。

blocks.en: A match made, the other hopefuls retire with the same deliberate indifference, and the selected cocks have their spurs (tadji) affixed- razor sharp, pointed steel swords, four or five inches long. This is a delicate job which only a small proportion of men, a half-dozen or so in most villages, know how to do properly. The man who attaches the spurs also provides them, and if the rooster he assists wins its owner awards him the spur-leg of the victim. The spurs are affixed by winding a long length of string around the foot of the spur and the leg of the cock. For reasons I shall come to, it is done somewhat differently from case to case, and is an obsessively deliberate affair. The lore about spurs is extensive-they are sharpened only at eclipses and the dark of the moon, should be kept out of the sight of women, and so forth. And they are handled, both in use and out, with the same curious combination of fussiness and sensuality the Balinese direct toward ritual objects generally.
blocks.zh: 比赛完成后，其他有希望的鸽子也以同样故意的冷漠态度退出，而被选中的雄鸽则被贴上马刺（tadji）——锋利的尖头钢剑，四五英寸长。这是一项微妙的工作，只有一小部分人（大多数村庄只有六人左右）知道如何正确完成。装马刺的人也会提供马刺，如果他协助的公鸡获胜，主人就会奖励他受害者的马刺腿。马刺是通过将一根长绳子缠绕在马刺的脚部和公鸡的腿上来固定的。出于我将要谈到的原因，不同情况的处理方式有所不同，并且是一件经过深思熟虑的事情。关于马刺的传说非常广泛——它们只有在日食和月黑时才会变得锋利，应该远离女性的视线，等等。无论是在使用中还是在使用中，它们的处理方式都与巴厘人对仪式物品的挑剔和感性的奇怪结合相同。

blocks.en: The spurs affixed, the two cocks are placed by their handlers (who may or may not be their owners) facing one another in the center of the ring. A coconut pierced with a small hole is placed in a pail of water, in which it takes about twenty-one seconds to sink, a period known as a tjeng and marked at beginning and end by the beating of a slit gong. During these twenty-one seconds the handlers (pengangkeb) are not permitted to touch their roosters. If, as sometimes happens, the animals have not fought during this time, they are picked up, fluffed, pulled, prodded, and otherwise insulted, and put back in the center of the ring and the process begins again. Sometimes they refuse to fight at all, or one keeps running away, in which case they are imprisoned together under a wicker cage, which usually gets them engaged.
blocks.zh: 固定好马刺后，两只雄鸽由它们的饲养员（可能是也可能不是它们的主人）面对面放置在赛场中央。将一个穿有小孔的椰子放入一桶水中，大约需要二十一秒的时间才能下沉，这一时期称为“tjeng”，在开始和结束时都会敲响缝锣。在这二十一秒内，饲养员（pengangkeb）不得触摸他们的公鸡。如果（有时会发生）动物在这段时间没有打斗，它们就会被抱起、蓬松、拉扯、刺戳或以其他方式侮辱，然后放回环的中心，然后这个过程再次开始。有时它们根本拒绝战斗，或者其中一个不断逃跑，在这种情况下，它们被一起囚禁在一个柳条笼子里，这通常会让它们交战。

blocks.en: Most of the time, in any case, the cocks fly almost immediately at one another in a wingbeating, head-thrusting, leg-kicking explosion of animal fury so pure, so absolute, and in its own way so beautiful, as to be almost abstract, a Platonic concept of hate. Within moments one or the other drives home a solid blow with his spur. The handler whose cock has delivered the blow immediately picks it up so that it will not get a return blow, for if he does not the match is likely to end in a mutually mortal tie as the two birds wildly hack each other to pieces. This is particularly true if, as often happens, the spur sticks in its victim's body, for then the aggressor is at the mercy of his wounded foe.
blocks.zh: 无论如何，大多数时候，公鸡几乎立即互相飞翔，以一种拍打翅膀、用头猛冲、用腿踢腿的方式爆发出动物的愤怒，如此纯粹、如此绝对，而且以其自己的方式如此美丽，几乎是抽象的，这是一种柏拉图式的仇恨概念。不一会儿，对方就用马刺狠狠地一击。被公鸡击中的训导员立即将其捡起来，这样它就不会受到反击，因为如果他不这样做，比赛很可能会以致命的平局结束，因为两只鸟会疯狂地将对方撕成碎片。如果像经常发生的那样，刺刺刺入受害者的身体，情况尤其如此，因为那时侵略者将受到他受伤的敌人的摆布。

blocks.en: With the birds again in the hands of their handlers, the coconut is now sunk three times after which the cock which has landed the blow must be set down to show that he is firm, a fact he demonstrates by wandering idly around the rink for a coconut sink. The coconut is then sunk twice more and the fight must recommence.
blocks.zh: 当鸽子再次回到它们的饲养员手中时，椰子会沉入三下，之后击中的雄鸡必须放下以表明他是坚定的，他通过在溜冰场闲逛寻找椰子沉降来证明这一事实。然后椰子又沉了两次，战斗必须重新开始。

blocks.en: During this interval, slightly over two minutes, the handler of the wounded cock has been working frantically over it, like a trainer patching a mauled boxer between rounds, to get it in shape for a last, desperate try for victory. He blows in its mouth, putting the whole chicken head in his own mouth and sucking and blowing, fluffs it, stuffs its wounds with various sorts of medicines, and generally tries anything he can think of to arouse the last ounce of spirit which may be hidden somewhere within it. By the time he is forced to put it back down he is usually drenched in chicken blood, but, as in prize fighting, a good handler is worth his weight in gold. Some of them can virtually make the dead walk, at least long enough for the second and final round.
blocks.zh: 在这段大约两分钟多一点的时间里，受伤公鸡的饲养员一直在疯狂地训练它，就像训练师在两轮比赛之间修补受伤的拳击手一样，让它恢复状态，为最后一次绝望的胜利而努力。他往它嘴里吹气，把整个鸡头放进自己嘴里吸吮吹气，把它弄松，用各种药物塞满它的伤口，通常会尝试任何他能想到的办法来唤起它可能隐藏在某处的最后一丝精神。当他被迫把它放回去时，他通常已经浑身是鸡血，但是，就像在职业拳击比赛中一样，一个好的驯手的价值与他的黄金相当。其中一些实际上可以让死人行走，至少足以进行第二轮和最后一轮。

blocks.en: In the climactic battle (if there is one; sometimes the wounded cock simply expires in the handler's hands or immediately as it is placed down again), the cock who landed the first blow usually proceeds to finish off his weakened opponent. But this is far from an inevitable outcome, for if a cock can walk he can fight, and if he can fight, he can kill, and what counts is which cock expires first. If the wounded one can get a stab in and stagger on until the other drops, he is the official winner, even if he himself topples over an instant later.
blocks.zh: 在激烈的战斗中（如果有的话；有时受伤的雄鸽会在训手手中死去，或者当它再次被放下时立即死去），首先击中的雄鸽通常会继续消灭他虚弱的对手。但这远非必然的结果，因为公鸡能走就可以打架，能打架就可以杀人，关键是哪只公鸡先死。如果受伤的一方能够被刺伤并摇摇晃晃地继续前进，直到另一方倒下，那么他就是正式的胜利者，即使他自己在一瞬间就倒下了。

blocks.en: Surrounding all this melodrama - which the crowd packed tight around the ring follows in near silence, moving their bodies in kinesthetic sympathy with the movement of the animals, cheering their champions on with wordless hand motions, shiftings of the shoulders, turnings of the head, falling back en masse as the cock with the murderous spurs careens toward one side of the ring (it is said that spectators sometimes lose eyes and fingers from being too attentive), surging forward again as they glance off toward another - is a vast body of extraordinarily elaborate and precisely detailed rules.
blocks.zh: 围绕着这一切的情节剧——观众紧紧地围在赛场周围，几乎一片寂静，他们的身体随着动物的运动而移动，用无言的手势、肩膀的移动、头部的转动为他们的冠军欢呼，当公鸡带着凶残的马刺向赛场的一侧倾斜时，他们集体向后倒去(据说观众有时会因为太专心而失去眼睛和手指)，再次向前涌动，他们向另一个人瞥了一眼——这是一大堆非常复杂和精确的规则。

blocks.en: These rules, together with the developed lore of cocks and cockfighting which accompanies them, are written down in palm leaf manuscripts (lontar; rontal) passed on from generation to generation as part of the general legal and cultural tradition of the villages. At a fight, the umpire (saja konong; djuru kembar) - the man who manages the coconut - is in charge of their application and his authority is absolute. I have never seen an umpire's judgment questioned on any subject, even by the more despondent losers, nor have I ever heard, even in private, a charge of unfairness directed against one, or, for that matter, complaints about umpires in general. Only exceptionally well-trusted, solid, and, given the complexity of the code, knowledgeable citizens perform this job, and in fact men will bring their cocks only to fights presided over by such men. It is also the umpire to whom accusations of cheating, which, though rare in the extreme, occasionally arise, are referred; and it is he who in the not infrequent cases where the cocks expire virtually together decides which (if either, for, though the Balinese do not care for such an outcome, there can be ties) went first. Likened to a judge, a king, a priest, and a policeman, he is all of these, and under his assured direction the animal passion of the fight proceeds within the civic certainty of the law. In the dozens of cockfights I saw in Bali, I never once saw an altercation about rules. Indeed, I never saw an open altercation, other than those between cocks, at all.

blocks.en: This crosswise doubleness of an event which, taken as a fact of nature, is rage untrammeled and, taken as a fact of culture, is form perfected, defines the cockfight as a sociological entity. A cockfight is what, searching for a name for something not vertebrate enough to be called a group and not structureless enough to be called a crowd, Erving Goffman has called a "focused gathering"-a set of persons engrossed in a common flow of activity and relating to one another in terms of that flow. Such gatherings meet and disperse; the participants in them fluctuate; the activity that focuses them is discreet-a particulate process that reoccurs rather than a continuous one that endures. They take their form from the situation that evokes them, the floor on which they are placed, as Goffman puts it; but it is a form, and an articulate one, nonetheless. For the situation, the floor is itself created, in jury deliberations, surgical operations, block meetings, sit-ins, cockfights, by the cultural preoccupations-here, as we shall see, the celebration of status rivalrywhich not only specify the focus but, assembling actors and arranging scenery, bring it actually into being.
blocks.zh: This crosswise doubleness of an event which, taken as a fact of nature, is rage untrammeled and, taken as a fact of culture, is form perfected, defines the cockfight as a sociological entity. A cockfight is what, searching for a name for something not vertebrate enough to be called a group and not structureless enough to be called a crowd, Erving Goffman has called a "focused gathering"-a set of persons engrossed in a common flow of activity and relating to one another in terms of that flow.这样的聚会，相遇又散去；参与者有波动；使他们集中注意力的活动是谨慎的——一种重复发生的微粒过程，而不是持续的连续过程。正如戈夫曼所说，它们的形式来自于唤起它们的情境，即它们所处的地板；但它仍然是一种形式，而且是一种清晰的形式。 For the situation, the floor is itself created, in jury deliberations, surgical operations, block meetings, sit-ins, cockfights, by the cultural preoccupations-here, as we shall see, the celebration of status rivalrywhich not only specify the focus but, assembling actors and arranging scenery, bring it actually into being.

blocks.en: In classical times (that is to say, prior to the Dutch invasion of 1908) when there were no bureaucrats around to improve popular morality, the staging of a cockfight was an explicitly societal matter. Bringing a cock to an important fight was, for an adult male, a compulsory duty of citizenship; taxation of fights, which were usually held on market day, was a major source of public revenue; patronage of the art was a stated responsibility of princes; and the cock ring, or wantilan, stood in the center of the village near those other monuments of Balinese civility-the council house, the origin temple, the marketplace, the signal tower, and the banyan tree. Today, a few special occasions aside, the newer rectitude makes so open a statement of the connection between the excitements of collective life and those of blood sport impossible, but, less directly expressed, the connection itself remains intimate and intact. To expose it, however, it is necessary to turn to the aspect of cockfighting around which all the others pivot, and through which they exercise their force, an aspect I have thus far studiously ignored. blocks.en: Odds and Even Money
blocks.zh: 赔率和赔率

blocks.en: The Balinese never do anything in a simple way that they can contrive to do in a complicated one, and to this generalization cockfight wagering is no exception.
blocks.zh: 巴厘人从不以简单的方式做任何事情，他们可以设法用复杂的方式来做，对于这一概括，斗鸡投注也不例外。

blocks.en: In the first place, there are two sorts of bets, or toh. There is the single axial bet in the center between the principals (toh ketengah), and there is the cloud of peripheral ones around the ring between members of the audience (toh kesasi ). The first is typically large; the second typically small. The first is collective, involving coalitions of bettors clustering around the owner; the second is individual, man to man. The first is a matter of deliberate, very quiet, almost furtive arrangement by the coalition members and the umpire huddled like conspirators in the center of the ring; the second is a matter of impulsive shouting, public offers, and public acceptances by the excited throng around its edges. And most curiously, and as we shall see most revealingly, where the first is always, without exception, even money, the second, equally without exception, is never such. What is a fair coin in the center is a biased one on the side.
blocks.zh: 首先，有两种赌注，或“toh”。校长之间的中心有单轴投注（toh ketengah），而观众成员之间的环周围有大量外围投注（toh kesasi）。第一个通常很大；第二个通常很小。第一个是集体的，包括聚集在所有者周围的投注者联盟；第二个是个人的，人与人之间的。第一个是联盟成员和裁判像阴谋家一样挤在赛场中央，经过深思熟虑、非常安静、几乎是偷偷摸摸的安排；第二个是边缘激动的人群冲动的叫喊、公开报价和公开接受的问题。最奇怪的是，正如我们将看到的最有启发性的那样，第一个总是无一例外地是金钱，而第二个同样无一例外地从来不是金钱。中间是公平的硬币，侧面是有偏差的。

blocks.en: The center bet is the official one, hedged in again with a webwork of rules, and is made between the two cock owners, with the umpire as overseer and public witness. This bet, which, as I say, is always relatively and sometimes very large, is never raised simply by the owner in whose name it is made, but by him together with four or five, sometimes seven or eight, allieskin, village mates, neighbors, close friends. He may, if he is not especially well-to-do, not even be the major contributor, though, if only to show that he is not involved in any chicanery, he must be a significant one.
blocks.zh: 中间投注是官方投注，再次受到一系列规则的限制，由两位雄鸡主人之间进行，裁判员作为监督者和公众见证人。正如我所说，这个赌注总是相对较大，有时甚至非常大，它从来不是由主人以自己的名义下的，而是由他和四五个，有时是七八个人，同乡，邻居，亲密的朋友一起下的。如果他不是特别富裕，他甚至可能不是主要贡献者，但是，如果只是为了表明他没有参与任何欺骗行为，他必须是一个重要的贡献者。

blocks.en: Of the fifty-seven matches for which I have exact and reliable data on the center bet, the range is from fifteen ringgits to five hundred, with a mean at eighty-five and with the distribution being rather noticeably trimodal: small fights (15 ringgits either side of 35 ) accounting for about 45 per cent of the total number; medium ones (20 ringgits either side of 70) for about 25 per side of 175) for about 20 per cent, with a few very small and very large of a manual laborer - a brickmaker, day, and considering the fact that fights were held on the average the immediate area I studied, this is clearly serious gambling, even if the bets are pooled rather than individual efforts.
blocks.zh: 在我掌握准确可靠的中注数据的 57 场比赛中，范围从 15 林吉特到 500 林吉特不等，平均为 85 林吉特，并且分布呈相当明显的三态：小规模斗殴（35 林吉特两边各 15 林吉特）约占总数的 45%；中等规模的（70林吉特两边各20林吉特）大约25林吉特（175林吉特）每边大约20％，还有一些非常小的和非常大的体力劳动者 - 砖匠，一天，考虑到我研究的附近地区平均发生打架斗殴的事实，这显然是严重的赌博，即使赌注是集中而不是个人努力。

blocks.en: The side bets are, however, something else altogether. Rather than the solemn, legalistic pactmaking of the center, wagering takes place rather in the fashion in which the stock exchange used to work when it was out on the curb. There is a fixed and known odds paradigm which runs in a continuous series from ten-tonine at the short end to two-to-one on the long: 10-9, 9-8, 8-7, 7-6, 6-5, 5-4, 4-3, 3-2, 2-1. The man who wants the underdog cock shouts the short-side number indicating the odds he wants to be given. That is, if he shouts gasal, "five," he wants the underdog at five-to-four (or, for him, four-to-five); if he shouts "four," he wants it at four-to-three (again, he putting up the "three"), if "nine" at nine-to-eight, and so on. A man backing the favorite, and thus considering giving odds if he can get them short enough, indicates the fact by crying out the color-type of that cock - "brown," "speckled," or whatever.
blocks.zh: 然而，附带的赌注完全是另一回事。 Rather than the solemn, legalistic pactmaking of the center, wagering takes place rather in the fashion in which the stock exchange used to work when it was out on the curb. There is a fixed and known odds paradigm which runs in a continuous series from ten-tonine at the short end to two-to-one on the long: 10-9, 9-8, 8-7, 7-6, 6-5, 5-4, 4-3, 3-2, 2-1.想要弱者雄鸡的男子喊出短边数字，表明他想要获得的赔率。也就是说，如果他喊加萨尔“五”，他希望失败者以五比四（或者，对他来说，四比五）；如果他喊“四”，他希望以四比三的比分（再次，他喊出“三”），如果他喊“九”，则以九比八的比分，依此类推。 A man backing the favorite, and thus considering giving odds if he can get them short enough, indicates the fact by crying out the color-type of that cock - "brown," "speckled," or whatever.

blocks.en: Almost always odds calling starts off toward the long end of the range - five-to-four or four-tothree- and then moves toward the shorter end with greater or less speed and to a greater and lesser degree. Men crying "five" and finding themselves answered only with cries of "brown" start crying "six." If the change is made and partners are still scarce, the procedure is repeated in a move to the cocks are clearly mismatched, there may be no upward movement very, very rarely to two-to-one, a shift which is accompanied by a upward is accompanied by an increasing number. But the general pattern is for the betting to move a . shorter or longer distance up the scale toward the, for sidebets, nonexistent pole of even money, with the overwhelming majority of bets falling in the four-to-three to eight-to-seven range.
blocks.zh: 赔率跟注几乎总是从范围的长端开始——五比四或四比三——然后以或大或慢的速度、或大或小的程度向短端移动。男人们喊“五”，发现自己只能喊“棕色”，于是开始喊“六”。如果进行了改变并且伙伴仍然稀缺，则在移动中重复该过程，直到雄鸽明显不匹配，可能没有向上移动，非常非常罕见地到二对一，伴随着向上的移动伴随着数量的增加。但一般模式是投注移动 。对于边注而言，无论是更短还是更长的距离，都不存在均等奖金的极点，绝大多数赌注落在四比三到八比七的范围内。

blocks.en: The higher the center bet, the more likely the match will in actual fact be an even one. In a large-bet fight the pressure to make the match a genuinely fifty-fifty proposition is enormous, and is consciously felt as such. For medium fights the pressure is somewhat less, and for small ones less yet, though there is always an effort to make things at least approximately equal, for even at fifteen ringgits (five days work) no one wants to make an even money bet in a clearly unfavorable situation. And, again, what statistics I have tend to bear this out. In my fifty-seven matches, the favorite won thirtythree times over-all, the underdog twenty-four, a 1.4 to 1 ratio. But if one splits the figures at sixty ringgits center bets, the ratios turn out to be 1.1 to 1 (twelve favorites, eleven underdogs) for those above this line, and 1.6 to 1 (twentyone and thirteen) for those below it. Or, if you take the extremes, for very large fights, those with center bets over a hundred ringgits the ratio is 1 to 1 (seven and seven); for very small fights, those under forty ringgits, it is 1.9 to 1 (nineteen and ten).
blocks.zh: 中心赌注越高，比赛实际上越有可能是平局。在一场大赌注的比赛中，让比赛成为真正的五五十的命题的压力是巨大的，并且是有意识地感受到的。对于中型比赛，压力要小一些，对于小型比赛来说压力还小，尽管总是努力使事情至少大致相等，因为即使是十五林吉特（五天工作），也没有人愿意在明显不利的情况下进行等额投注。再说一次，我掌握的统计数据也证实了这一点。在我的 57 场比赛中，热门球队总共赢了 3​​3 场，劣势球队赢了 24 场，比例为 1.4 比 1。但如果将数字分成六十令吉的中心投注，那么对于高于此线的玩家，比率为 1.1 比 1（十二个热门，十一个失败者），对于低于此线的玩家，比率为 1.6 比 1（二十一和十三）。或者，如果你采取极端的方式，对于非常大的战斗，那些中心赌注超过一百令吉的人，比率是1比1（七加七）；对于非常小的战斗，即四十令吉以下的战斗，比例为 1.9 比 1（十九和十）。

blocks.en: The paradox of fair coin in the middle, biased coin on the outside is thus a merely apparent one. The two betting systems, though formally incongruent, are not really contradictory to one another, but part of a single larger system in which the center bet is, so to speak, the "center of gravity," drawing, the larger it is the more so, the outside bets toward the short-odds end of the scale. The center bet thus "makes the game," or perhaps better, defines it, signals what, following a notion of Jeremy Bentham's, I am going to call its "depth."
blocks.zh: 因此，“中间是公平的硬币，外面是有偏差的硬币”的悖论只是一个表面现象。这两个投注系统虽然形式上不一致，但实际上并不矛盾，而是一个更大系统的一部分，可以说，中心投注是“重心”，越大，外围投注越倾向于小赔率端。因此，中心赌注“创造了游戏”，或者更好地定义了游戏，标志着什么，按照杰里米·边沁的概念，我将称之为“深度”。

blocks.en: The Balinese attempt to create an interesting, if you will, "deep," match by making the center bet as large as possible so that the cocks matched will be as equal and as fine as possible, and the outcome, thus, as unpredictable as possible. They do not always succeed. Nearly half the matches are relatively trivial, relatively uninteresting-in my borrowed terminology, "shallow"- affairs. But that fact no more argues against my interpretation than the fact that most painters, poets, and playwrights are mediocre argues against the view that artistic effort is directed toward profundity and, with a certain frequency, approximates it. The image of artistic technique is indeed exact: the center bet is a means, a device, for creating "interesting," "deep" matches, not the reason, or at least not the main reason, why they are interesting, the source of their fascination, the substance of their depth. The question why such matches are interesting-indeed, for the Balinese, exquisitely absorbing-takes us out of the realm of formal concerns into more broadly sociological and social-psychological ones, and to a less purely economic idea of what "depth" in gaming amounts to.
blocks.zh: 巴厘人试图通过使中心赌注尽可能大来创造一场有趣的，如果你愿意的话，“深度”的比赛，这样匹配的雄鸽将尽可能平等和尽可能好，因此结果也尽可能不可预测。他们并不总是成功。近一半的比赛都是相对琐碎、相对无趣的——用我借用的术语来说，“肤浅”——事务。但这个事实并没有更多地反驳我的解释，就像大多数画家、诗人和剧作家都是平庸的事实反驳这样一种观点，即艺术的努力是指向深刻的，并且以一定的频率接近它。艺术技巧的形象确实是准确的：中心赌注是一种手段、一种装置，用于创造“有趣的”、“深刻的”匹配，而不是它们有趣的原因，或者至少不是主要原因，它们的魅力的源泉，它们的深度的实质。为什么这样的比赛很有趣——事实上，对于巴厘人来说，非常吸引人——这个问题让我们脱离了正式关注的领域，进入了更广泛的社会学和社会心理学领域，以及对游戏“深度”意味着什么的不那么纯粹的经济概念。

blocks.en: Playing with Fire
blocks.zh: 玩火

blocks.en: Bentham's concept of "deep play" is found in his The Theory of Legislation. By it he means play in which the stakes are so high that it is, from his utilitarian standpoint, irrational for men to engage in it at all.
blocks.zh: 边沁的“深层游戏”概念可以在他的《立法理论》中找到。他所说的游戏是指赌注如此之高的游戏，从他的功利主义观点来看，人们参与其中根本不合理。

blocks.en: This, I must stress immediately, is not to say that the money does not matter, or that the Balinese is no more concerned about losing five hundred ringgits than fifteen. Such a conclusion would be absurd. It is because money does, in this hardly unmaterialistic society, matter and matter very much that the more of it one risks the more of a lot of other things, such as one's pride, one's poise, one's dispassion, one's masculinity, one also risks, again only momentarily but again very publicly as well. In deep cockfights an owner and his collaborators, and, as we shall see, to a lesser but still quite real extent also their backers on the outside, put their money where their status is.
blocks.zh: 我必须立即强调，这并不是说钱不重要，或者巴厘人对损失五百林吉特并不比损失十五林吉特更担心。这样的结论是荒谬的。正是因为金钱在这个几乎非物质主义的社会里确实非常重要，所以一个人所冒的风险越多，其他很多东西的风险就越大，比如一个人的骄傲、一个人的镇定、一个人的冷静、一个人的男子气概，一个人也会冒风险，同样只是暂时的，但也是非常公开的。在深入的斗鸡中，斗鸡的主人和他的合作者，以及我们将看到的，在较小但仍然相当真实的程度上，还有他们的外部支持者，将他们的钱花在了他们的地位上。

blocks.en: It is in large part because the marginal disutility of loss is so great at the higher levels of betting that to engage in such betting is to lay one's public self, allusively and metaphorically, through the medium of one's cock, on the line. And though to a Benthamite this might seem merely to increase the irrationality of the enterprise that much further, to the Balinese what it mainly increases is the meaningfulness of it all. And as (to follow Weber rather than Bentham) the imposition of meaning on life is the major end and primary condition of human existence, that access of significance more than compensates for the economic costs involved. Actually, given the even-money quality of the larger matches, important changes in material fortune among those who regularly participate in them seem virtually nonexistent, because matters more or less even out over the long run.
blocks.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为在较高水平的投注中，损失的边际负效用是如此之大，以至于从事这种投注就是通过暗示和隐喻的方式，通过一个人的鸡巴的媒介，将一个人的公共自我置于赌注之上。尽管对边沁主义者来说，这似乎只是进一步增加了企业的非理性，但对巴厘人来说，它主要增加的是这一切的意义。而且（遵循韦伯而不是边沁的观点）赋予生命意义是人类存在的主要目的和首要条件，获得意义的意义远远超过了所涉及的经济成本的补偿。事实上，考虑到大型比赛的均等奖金质量，那些经常参加比赛的人在物质财富上的重大变化似乎几乎不存在，因为从长远来看，或多或少都重要。

blocks.en: This graduated correlation of "status gambling" with deeper fights and, inversely, "money gambling" with shallower ones is in fact quite general. Bettors themselves form a sociomoral hierarchy in these terms. As noted earlier, at most cockfights there are, around the very edges of the cockfight area, a large number of mindless, sheer-chance type gambling games (roulette, dice throw, coin-spin, pea-under-theshell) operated by concessionaires. Only women, children, adolescents, and various other sorts of people who do not (or not yet) fight cocks - the extremely poor, the socially despised, the personally idiosyncratic - play at these games, at, of course, penny ante levels. Cockfighting men would be ashamed to go anywhere near them. Slightly above these people in standing are those who, though they do not themselves fight cocks, bet on the smaller matches around the edges. Next, there are those who fight cocks in small, or occasionally medium matches, but have not the status to join in the large ones, though they may bet from time to time on the side in those. And finally, there are those, the really substantial members of the community, the solid citizenry around whom local life revolves, who fight in the larger fights and bet on them around the side. The focusing element in these focused gatherings, these men generally dominate and define the sport as they dominate and define the society. When a Balinese male talks, in that almost venerative way, about "the true cockfighter," the bebatoh ("bettor" ) or djuru kurung ("cage keeper"), it is this sort of person, not those who bring the mentality of the pea-and-shell game into the quite different, inappropriate context of the cockfight, the driven gambler (potet, a word which has the secondary meaning of thief or reprobate), and the wistful hanger-on, that they mean. For such a man, what is really going on in a match is something rather closer to an affaire d'honneur (though, with the Balinese talent for practical fantasy, the blood that is spilled is only figuratively human) than to the stupid, mechanical crank of a slot machine.
blocks.zh: “地位赌博”与较深的争斗以及相反的“金钱赌博”与较浅的争斗的这种渐进相关性实际上是相当普遍的。从这些角度来看，博彩者本身就形成了社会道德等级制度。如前所述，在大多数斗鸡活动中，在斗鸡区域的边缘，都有大量由特许经营者经营的无意识的、纯粹碰运气的赌博游戏（轮盘赌、掷骰子、转硬币、壳下豌豆）。只有妇女、儿童、青少年和其他各种不（或尚未）斗鸡的人——赤贫者、社会鄙视者、个人特质——玩这些游戏，当然，赌注水平很低。斗鸡的人会羞于靠近它们。地位稍高于这些人的是那些虽然自己不斗鸡但在边缘较小的比赛上下注的人。其次，还有一些人在小型比赛中斗鸡，或者偶尔在中型比赛中斗鸡，但没有资格参加大型比赛，尽管他们可能偶尔会在这些比赛中下注。最后，还有一些人，社区中真正重要的成员，当地生活围绕着他们的坚实公民，他们参加更大的战斗，并在他们周围下注。这些男性是这些集中聚会中的焦点元素，他们通常主导和定义这项运动，就像他们主导和定义社会一样。当巴厘岛男性以一种近乎崇敬的方式谈论“真正的斗鸡者”、bebatoh（“赌徒”）或 djuru kurung（“笼子看守者”）时，他就是这类人，而不是那些将豌豆和贝壳游戏的心态带入完全不同的、不恰当的斗鸡背景中的人，即被驱使的赌徒（potet，这个词具有小偷或小偷的次要含义）。被遗弃的人），以及他们所说的渴望的追随者。对于这样的人来说，比赛中真正发生的事情更接近于一场荣誉事件（尽管巴厘人具有实际幻想的天赋，所流的鲜血只是象征性的人类）而不是老虎机上愚蠢的机械曲柄。

blocks.en: What makes Balinese cockfighting deep is thus not money in itself, but what, the more of it that is involved the more so, money causes to happen: the migration of the Balinese status hierarchy into the body of the cockfight. Psychologically an Aesopian representation of the ideal/demonic, rather narcissistic, male self, sociologically it is an equally Aesopian representation of the complex fields of tension set up by the controlled, muted, ceremonial, but for all that deeply felt, interaction of those selves in the context of everyday life. The cocks may be surrogates for their owners' personalities, animal mirrors of psychic form, but the cockfight is - or more exactly, deliberately is made to be - a simulation of the social matrix, the involved system of crosscutting, overlapping, highly corporate groups --villages, kingroups, irrigation societies, temple congregations, "castes" - in which its devotees live. And as prestige, the necessity to affirm it, defend it, celebrate it, justify it, and just plain bask in it (but not given the strongly ascriptive character of Balinese stratification, to seek it), is perhaps the central driving force in the society, so also ambulant penises, blood sacrifices, and monetary exchanges aside - is it of the cockfight. This apparent amusement and seeming sport is, to take another phrase from Erving Goffman, "a status bloodbath."
blocks.zh: 因此，巴厘岛斗鸡之所以深入人心，并不是金钱本身，而是金钱导致的结果：巴厘岛的地位等级制度迁移到了斗鸡的主体中。从心理学上来说，这是对理想/恶魔般的、相当自恋的男性自我的伊索式表征；从社会学上来说，它同样是对由受控的、沉默的、仪式性的、但尽管有深刻感受的自我在日常生活背景下的互动所建立的复杂紧张场的伊索式表征。公鸡可能是主人个性的代表，是精神形态的动物镜子，但斗鸡是——或者更准确地说，是故意制造的——社会矩阵的模拟，涉及交叉、重叠、高度企业化的群体体系——村庄、亲属群体、灌溉协会、寺庙集会、“种姓”——斗鸡的信徒生活在其中。作为声望，肯定它、捍卫它、庆祝它、证明它的正当性以及简单地享受它的必要性（但不考虑巴厘岛分层的强烈归属特征，去寻求它），也许是社会的核心驱动力，所以除了流动的阴茎、血祭和货币交换之外，斗鸡也是如此。用欧文·戈夫曼的另一句话来说，这种表面上的娱乐和表面上的运动是“一场地位大屠杀”。

blocks.en: The easiest way to make this clear, and at least to some degree to demonstratee it, is to invoke the village whose cockfighting activities I observed the closest - the one in which the raid occurred and from which my statistical data are taken.
blocks.zh: 要阐明这一点，至少在某种程度上证明这一点，最简单的方法是援引我观察到最接近斗鸡活动的村庄——袭击发生的那个村庄，我的统计数据就是从那个村庄获取的。

blocks.en: Consider, then, as support of the general thesis that the cockfight, and especially the deep cockfight, is fundamentally a dramatization of status concerns, the following facts:
blocks.zh: 那么，为了支持斗鸡，尤其是深度斗鸡，从根本上来说是对地位问题的戏剧化这一一般论点，请考虑以下事实：

blocks.en: 1. A man virtually never bets against a cock owned by a member of his own kingroup. Usually he will feel obliged to bet for it, the more so the closer the kin tie and the deeper the fight. If he is certain in his mind that it will not win, he may just not bet at all, particularly if it is only a second cousin's bird or if the fight is a shallow one. But as a rule he will feel he must support it and, in deep games, nearly always does. Thus the great majority of the people calling "five" or "speckled" so demonstratively are expressing their allegiance to their kinsman, not their evaluation of his bird, their understanding of probability theory, or even their hopes of unearned income.
blocks.zh: 1. 一个人实际上从不打赌自己亲属拥有的公鸡。通常，他会觉得有必要为此下注，而且血缘关系越密切，争斗越激烈，他就越是如此。如果他心里确信这只鸽子不会赢，他可能根本就不会下注，特别是当这只鸽子是二表弟的鸽子或者比赛很浅的时候。但通常来说，他会觉得自己必须支持它，而且在深度比赛中，几乎总是如此。因此，绝大多数人如此明确地称呼“五”或“斑点”是在表达他们对亲戚的忠诚，而不是他们对他的鸟的评价，他们对概率论的理解，甚至他们对不劳而获的收入的希望。

blocks.en: 2. This principle is extended logically. If your kin group is not involved you will support an allied kingroup against an unallied one in the same way, and so on through the very involved networks of alliances which, as I say, make up this, as any other, Balinese village.
blocks.zh: 2. 这一原则得到了逻辑上的扩展。如果你的亲属团体没有参与其中，你将以同样的方式支持一个结盟的亲属团体对抗一个不结盟的亲属团体，等等，通过非常复杂的联盟网络，正如我所说，这些联盟网络构成了这个，就像任何其他巴厘岛村庄一样。

blocks.en: 3. So, too, for the village as a whole. If an outsider cock is fighting any cock from your village you will tend to support the local one. If, what is a rarer circumstance but occurs every now and then, a cock from outside your cockfight circuit is fighting one inside it you will also tend to support the "home bird."
blocks.zh: 3. 对于整个村庄来说也是如此。如果一只外地公鸡与你村里的任何一只公鸡战斗，你会倾向于支持本地公鸡。如果，一种比较罕见但时常发生的情况，一只来自斗鸡场外的公鸡正在与场内的另一只公鸡打斗，你也会倾向于支持“家鸟”。

blocks.en: 4. Cocks which come from any distance are almost always favorites, for the theory is the man would not have dared to bring it if it was not a good cock, the more so the further he has come. His followers are, of course, obliged to support him, and when the more grand-scale legal cockfights are held (on holidays and so on) the people of the village take what they regard to be the best cocks in the village, regardless of ownership, and go off to support them, although they will almost certainly have to give odds on them and to make large bets to show that they are not a cheapskate village. Actually, such "away games," though infrequent, tend to mend the ruptures between village members that the constantly occurring "home games," where village factions are opposed rather than united, exacerbate.
blocks.zh: 4.来自任何距离的雄鸡几乎总是最受欢迎的，因为理论上来说，如果不是好雄鸡，男人就不敢带它，而且他来得越远，就越不敢带它来。当然，他的追随者有义务支持他，当举行更大规模的合法斗鸡活动时（节假日等），村里的人会挑选他们认为是村里最好的公鸡，不管所有权如何，然后去支持它们，尽管他们几乎肯定要给它们下注，并下大赌注，以表明他们不是一个小气的村庄。事实上，这种“客场比赛”虽然不常见，但往往会弥合村民之间的裂痕，而不断发生的“主场比赛”则加剧了村里各派对立而不是团结的关系。

blocks.en: 5. Almost all matches are sociologically relevant. You seldom get two outsider cocks fighting, or two cocks with no particular group backing, or with group backing which is mutually unrelated in any clear way. When you do get them, the game is very shallow, betting very slow, and the whole thing very dull, with no one save the immediate principals and an addict gambler or two at all interested.
blocks.zh: 5. 几乎所有匹配都具有社会学相关性。你很少会看到两只外来的公鸡打架，或者两只没有特定群体支持的公鸡打架，或者得到的群体支持在任何明显的方式上都没有相互关联。当你真正得到它们时，游戏非常浅薄，下注非常缓慢，整个事情非常乏味，除了直接的校长和一两个上瘾的赌徒之外没有人感兴趣。

blocks.en: 6. By the same token, you rarely get two cocks from the same group, even more rarely from the same subfaction, and virtually never from the same sub-subfaction (which would be in most cases one extended family) fighting. Similarly, in outside village fights two members of the village will rarely fight against one another, even though, as bitter rivals, they would do so with enthusiasm on their home grounds.
blocks.zh: 6. 出于同样的原因，你很少会看到两只来自同一群体的雄鸽，更罕见的是来自同一亚派系的雄鸽，而且几乎从来不会来自同一亚亚派系（在大多数情况下是一个大家庭）的斗鸡。同样，在村外打架时，两个村里的人很少会互相打斗，尽管作为死对头，他们会在自己的土地上热情地这样做。

blocks.en: 7. On the individual level, people involved in an institutionalized hostility relationship, called puik, in which they do not speak or otherwise have anything to do with each other (the causes of this formal breaking of relations are many: wife-capture, inheritance arguments, political differences) will bet very heavily, sometimes almost maniacally, against one another in what is a frank and direct attack on the very masculinity, the ultimate ground of his status, of the opponent.
blocks.zh: 7. 在个人层面上，陷入一种制度化的敌对关系（称为“puik”）的人们，在这种关系中，他们彼此之间不说话或没有任何关系（这种正式关系破裂的原因有很多：夺妻、遗产争论、政治分歧），他们会非常激烈地、有时甚至近乎疯狂地相互下注，坦率而直接地攻击对手的男子气概，即他的地位的最终基础。

blocks.en: 8. The center bet coalition is, in all but the shallowest games, always made up by structural allies - no "outside money" is involved. What is "outside" depends upon the context, of course, but given it, no outside money is mixed in with the main bet; if the principals cannot raise it, it is not made. The center bet, again especially in deeper games, is thus the most direct and open expression of social opposition, which is one of the reasons why both it and match making are unease, furtiveness, embarrassment, and so on.
blocks.zh: 8. 除了最浅的游戏外，中心投注联盟总是由结构性盟友组成 - 不涉及“外部资金”。当然，什么是“外部”取决于具体情况，但考虑到这一点，主要赌注中不会混入外部资金；如果校长不能提出，就不会制定。因此，中注，特别是在更深层次的游戏中，是社会对立最直接、最公开的表达，这也是中注和配对都令人不安、鬼祟、尴尬等的原因之一。

blocks.en: 9. The rule about borrowing
blocks.zh: 9. 借用规则

blocks.en: (and the Balinese are quite the economic mercy of your enemy that way. Gambling on a rather short-term basis, are always to friends, never to irrelevant or neutral so far as you are concerned (though, as are to each other) you do not even ask a relative or a friend whom he is betting on, because if you know how he is betting and he knows you know, and you go the other way, it will lead to strain. This rule is explicit and rigid; fairly elaborate, even rather artificial precautions are taken to avoid breaking it. At the very least you must pretend not to notice what he is doing, and he what you are doing.
blocks.zh: （巴厘人在这方面对你的敌人在经济上很仁慈。赌博是在相当短期的基础上，总是对朋友来说，就你们而言，永远不要无关紧要或中立（尽管，就像彼此一样），你甚至不会问亲戚或朋友他在谁身上下注，因为如果你知道他如何下注，他知道你知道，而你走另一条路，就会导致紧张。这条规则是明确和严格的；相当详细，甚至采取了人为的预防措施至少你必须假装没有注意到他在做什么，以及他在做什么。

blocks.en: 11. There is a special word for betting against the grain, which is also the word for "pardon me" (mpura). It is considered a bad thing to do, though if the center bet is small it is sometimes all right as long as you do not do it too often. But the larger the bet and the more frequently you do it, the more the "pardon me" tack will lead to social disruption.
blocks.zh: 11. 有一个特殊的词来表示对赌，这也是“请原谅我”（mpura）的词。这被认为是一件坏事，但如果中心赌注很小，有时只要你不经常这样做就可以。但赌注越大，赌注越频繁，“请原谅我”策略就越会导致社会混乱。

blocks.en: 12. In fact, the institutionalized hostility relation, puik, is often formally initiated (though its causes always lie elsewhere) by such a "pardon me" bet in a deep fight, putting the symbolic fat in the fire. Similarly, the end of such a normal social intercourse is often signalized (but, again, not actually brought about) by one or the other of the enemies supporting the other's bird.
blocks.zh: 12. 事实上，制度化的敌对关系（puik）常常是通过在一场激烈的战斗中“请原谅我”下注而正式引发的（尽管其原因总是在其他地方），将象征性的脂肪投入火中。类似地，这种正常社交交往的结束通常是由敌人中的一个或另一个支持另一只鸟而发出的信号（但同样，这并不是实际发生的）。

blocks.en: 13. In sticky, cross-loyalty situations, of which in this extraordinarily complex social system there are of course many, where a man is caught equally balanced loyalties, he tends to wander off for a cup of coffee or something to avoid having to bet, a form of behavior reminiscent of that of American voters in similar situations.
blocks.zh: 13. 在这个极其复杂的社会体系中，这种情况当然有很多，在这种粘性的、交叉忠诚的情况下，一个人在忠诚度相等的情况下，往往会去喝杯咖啡或其他东西，以避免必须下注，这种行为让人想起美国选民在类似情况下的行为。

blocks.en: 14. The people involved in the center bet are, especially in deep fights, virtually always leading members of their group-kinship, village, or whatever. Further, those who bet on the side (including these people) are, as I have already remarked, the more established members of the village - the solid citizens. Cockfighting is for those who are involved in the everyday politics of prestige as well, not for youth, women, subordinates, and so forth.
blocks.zh: 14. 参与中心赌注的人，尤其是在激烈的战斗中，实际上总是领导着他们的团体（亲属、村庄或其他团体）的成员。此外，正如我已经说过的，那些旁观者（包括这些人）是村里更有地位的成员——可靠的公民。斗鸡也适合那些参与日常声望政治的人，而不适合年轻人、妇女、下属等。

blocks.en: 15. So far as money is concerned, the explicitly expressed attitude toward it is that it is a secondary matter. It is not, as I have said, of no importance; Balinese are no happier to lose several weeks' income than anyone else. But they mainly look on the monetary aspects of the cockfight as self-balancing, a matter of just moving money around, circulating it among a fairly well-defined group of serious cockfighters. The really important wins and losses are seen mostly in other terms, and the general attitude toward wagering is not any hope of cleaning up, of making a killing (addict gamblers again excepted), but that of the horseplayer's prayer: "Oh, God, please let me break even." In prestige terms, however, you do not want to break even, but, in a momentary, punctuate sort of way, win utterly. The talk (which goes on all the time) is about fights against such-and-such a cock of So-and-So which your cock demolished, not on how much you won, a fact people, even for large bets, rarely remember for any length of time, though they will remember the day they did in Pan Loh's finest cock for years.
blocks.zh: 15. 就金钱而言，明确表达的态度是，它是次要的。正如我所说，这并非不重要；而是重要的。巴厘人对于失去几周的收入并不比其他人更高兴。但他们主要认为斗鸡的金钱方面是自我平衡的，只是转移金钱，在一群相当明确的严肃斗鸡者中流通。真正重要的输赢大多是通过其他方式来看待的，而人们对下注的普遍态度并不是希望能够干净利落、大赚一笔（赌徒上瘾的人除外），而是赌马者的祈祷：“哦，上帝，请让我收支平衡。”然而，就声望而言，你不想收支平衡，而是想以一种短暂的、间断的方式彻底获胜。谈话（一直在进行）是关于与某某公鸡的战斗，你的公鸡摧毁了，而不是你赢了多少，事实上，即使是大赌注，人们也很少记得很长一段时间，尽管他们会记得他们多年来用潘洛最好的公鸡比赛的那一天。

blocks.en: 16. You must bet on cocks of your own group aside from mere loyalty considerations, for if you do not people generally will say, "What! Is he too proud for the likes of us? Does he have to go to Java or Den Pasar [the capital town] to bet, he is such an important man?" Thus there is a general pressure to bet not only to show that you are important locally, but that you are not so important that you look down on everyone else as unfit even to be rivals. Similarly, home team people must bet against outside cocks or the outsiders will accuse it - a serious charge of just collecting entry fees and not really being interested in cockfighting, as well as again being arrogant and insulting.
blocks.zh: 16. 除了纯粹的忠诚度考虑之外，你还必须押注在自己组的雄鸽上，因为如果你不这样做，人们通常会说：“什么！他对我们这样的人来说太骄傲了吗？他必须去爪哇或登巴萨（首都）才能下注吗？他是如此重要的人物？”因此，人们普遍面临着打赌的压力，不仅是为了表明自己在当地很重要，而且还没有重要到看不起其他人，甚至认为自己不适合成为竞争对手。同样，主队的人必须与外面的公鸡打赌，否则外面的人会指责这种行为——这是一种严重的指控，因为他们只是收取入场费，而不是真正对斗鸡感兴趣，并且再次表现出傲慢和侮辱性。

blocks.en: 17. Finally, the Balinese peasants themselves are quite aware of all this and can and, at least to an ethnographer, do state most of it in approximately the same terms as I have.
blocks.zh: 17. 最后，巴厘岛农民自己非常清楚这一切，并且能够并且至少对于民族志学者来说确实能够用与我大致相同的术语来表述其中的大部分内容。

blocks.en: Fighting cocks, almost every Balinese I have ever discussed the subject with has said, is like playing with fire only not getting burned. You activate village and kingroup rivalries and hostilities, but in "play" form, coming dangerously and entrancingly close to the expression of open and direct interpersonal and intergroup aggression (something which, again, almost never happens in the normal course of ordinary life), but not quite, because, after all, it is "only a cockfight."
blocks.zh: 几乎所有与我讨论过这个话题的巴厘人都说，斗鸡就像玩火，只是不会被烧伤。你激发了村庄和亲属群体的竞争和敌对行动，但以“游戏”的形式，危险而令人着迷地接近公开和直接的人际和群体间攻击的表达（这在日常生活的正常过程中几乎从未发生过），但又不完全是，因为毕竟，这“只是一场斗鸡”。

blocks.en: More observations of this sort could be advanced, but perhaps the general point is, if not made, at least well-delineated, and the whole argument thus far can be usefully summarized in a formal paradigm:
blocks.zh: 可以提出更多此类观察，但也许一般观点即使没有提出，至少也得到了很好的描述，并且迄今为止的整个论点可以用一个正式的范式有效地总结：

blocks.en: THE MORE A MATCH IS . . .
blocks.zh: 匹配越多。 。 。

blocks.en: 1. Between near status equals (and/or personal enemies)
blocks.zh: 1. 地位接近的平等者（和/或个人敌人）之间

blocks.en: 2. Between high status individuals
blocks.zh: 2.地位高的人之间

blocks.en: THE DEEPER THE MATCH.
blocks.zh: 比赛越深入。

blocks.en: THE DEEPER THE MATCH IS
blocks.zh: 比赛越深入

blocks.en: 1. The closer the identification of cock and man (or: more properly, the deeper the match the more the man will advance his best, most closely-identified-with cock).
blocks.zh: 1. 雄鸽和男子的认同越接近（或者：更准确地说，匹配越深入，男子就越能提升他最好的、与雄鸽最接近的认同）。

blocks.en: 2. The finer the cocks involved and the more exactly they will be matched.
blocks.zh: 2. 参与的雄鸽越优秀，它们的匹配就越精确。

blocks.en: 3. The greater the emotion that will be involved and the more the general absorption in the match.
blocks.zh: 3. 涉及的情绪越大，比赛的整体投入程度也越高。

blocks.en: 4. The higher the individual bets center and outside, the shorter the outside bet odds will tend to be, and the more betting there will be over-all.
blocks.zh: 4. 中心和外围的个别投注越高，外围投注赔率往往越小，整体投注也越多。

blocks.en: 5. The less an economic and the more a "status" view of gaming will be involved, and the "solider" the citizens who will be gaming.
blocks.zh: 5. 游戏涉及的经济因素越少，“地位”观点就越多，参与游戏的公民就越“团结”。

blocks.en: Inverse arguments hold for the shallower the fight, culminating, in a reversed-signs sense, in the coin-spinning and dice-throwing amusements. For deep fights there are no absolute upper limits, though there are of course practical ones, and there are a great many legend-like tales of great Duel-in-the-Sun combats between lords and princes in classical times (for cockfighting has always been as much an elite concern as a popular one), far deeper than anything anyone, even aristocrats, could produce today anywhere in Bali.
blocks.zh: 反向论证适用于较浅的战斗，从反向符号的意义上来说，最终以转硬币和掷骰子的娱乐方式达到高潮。对于深入的战斗来说，虽然有实际的上限，但没有绝对的上限，并且有许多古典时代领主和王子之间伟大的阳光下决斗的传奇般的故事（因为斗鸡一直是精英关注的话题，也是大众关注的话题），其深度远远超出了当今巴厘岛任何地方的任何人，甚至是贵族，所能创造的。

blocks.en: Indeed, one of the great culture heroes of Bali is a prince, called after his passion for the sport, "The Cockfighter," who happened to be away at a very deep cockfight with a neighboring prince when the whole of his family-father, brothers, wives, sisters-were assassinated by commoner usurpers. Thus spared, he returned to dispatch the upstarts, regain the throne, reconstitute the Balinese high tradition, and build its most powerful, glorious, and prosperous state. Along with everything else that the Balinese see in fighting cocks-themselves, their social order, abstract hatred, masculinity, demonic power-they also see the archetype of status virtue, the arrogant, resolute, honor-mad player with real fire, the ksatria prince.
blocks.zh: 事实上，巴厘岛最伟大的文化英雄之一是一位王子，因其对这项运动的热情而被称为“斗鸡者”，当他的全家——父亲、兄弟、妻子、姐妹——被平民篡夺者暗杀时，他恰好在与邻近的一位王子进行一场激烈的斗鸡比赛。如此幸免于难，他回来消灭暴发户，重新夺回王位，重建巴厘岛的崇高传统，并建立其最强大、光荣和繁荣的国家。除了巴厘人在斗鸡中看到的一切——他们自己、他们的社会秩序、抽象的仇恨、男子气概、恶魔的力量——他们还看到了地位美德的原型，傲慢、坚决、为荣誉而疯狂的真正的火力选手，卡萨特里亚王子。

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en: What sets the cockfight apart from the ordinary course of life, lifts it from the realm of everyday practical affairs, and surrounds it with an aura of enlarged importance is not, as functionalist sociology would have it, that it reinforces status discriminations (such reinforcement is hardly necessary in a society where every act proclaims them), but that it provides a metasocial commentary upon the whole matter of assorting human beings into fixed hierarchical ranks and then organizing the major part of collective existence around that assortment. Its function, if you want to call it that, is interpretive: it is a Balinese reading of Balinese experience; a story they tell themselves about themselves.
blocks.zh: 使斗鸡区别于日常生活、将其从日常实际事务领域中抽离出来、并赋予它更大重要性的光环的，并不是像功能主义社会学所认为的那样，它强化了地位歧视（在一个每项行为都宣扬地位歧视的社会中，这种强化几乎是不必要的），而是它为将人类划分为固定的等级等级，然后围绕这种分类组织集体存在的主要部分的整个问题提供了一种元社会评论。如果你想这样称呼它的话，它的功能是解释性的：它是对巴厘岛经验的巴厘岛式解读；他们讲述自己的故事。

blocks.en: What the cockfight says it says in a vocabulary of sentiment-the thrill of risk, the despair of loss, the pleasure of triumph. Yet what it says is not merely that risk is exciting, loss depressing, or triumph gratifying, banal tautologies of affect, but that it is of these emotions, thus exampled, that society is built and individuals put together. Attending cockfights and participating in them is, for the Balinese, a kind of sentimental education. What he learns there is what his culture's ethos and his private sensibility (or, anyway, certain aspects of them) look like when spelled out externally in a collective text; that the two are near enough alike to be articulated in the symbolics of a single such text; and-the disquieting part-that the text in which this revelation is accomplished consists of a chicken hacking another mindlessly to bits.
blocks.zh: 斗鸡所表达的内容是一种情感词汇——冒险的兴奋、失败的绝望、胜利的喜悦。然而，它所说的不仅仅是风险令人兴奋，损失令人沮丧，或胜利令人欣慰，情感的平庸同义反复，而且正是这些情感，如此例证，社会得以建立，个人聚集在一起。观看斗鸡并参与其中，对于巴厘人来说，是一种情感教育。他在那里学到的是他的文化的精神和他的私人情感（或者无论如何，它们的某些方面）在集体文本中外部阐明时的样子；两者非常相似，可以用一个这样的文本的象征意义来表达；令人不安的是，完成这一启示的文本是一只鸡无意识地把另一只鸡砍成碎片。

blocks.en: Every people, the proverb has it, loves its own form of violence, The cockfight is the Balinese reflection on theirs: on its look, its uses, its force, its fascination. Drawing on almost every level of Balinese experience, it brings together themes-animal savagery, male narcissism, opponent gambling, status rivalry, mass excitement, blood sacrifice-whose main connection is their involvement with rage and the fear of rage, and, binding them into a set of rules which at once contains them and allows them play, builds a symbolic structure in which, over and over again, the reality of their inner affiliation can be intelligibly felt. If, to quote Northrop Frye again, we go to see Macbeth to learn what a man feels like after he has gained a kingdom and lost his soul, Balinese go to cockfights to find out what a man, usually composed, aloof, almost obsessively selfabsorbed, a kind of moral autocosm, feels like when, attacked, tormented, challenged, insulted, and driven in result to the extremes of fury, he has totally triumphed or been brought totally low.
blocks.zh: 俗话说，每个民族都喜欢自己的暴力形式，斗鸡是巴厘人对他们的暴力的反映：它的外观、它的用途、它的力量和它的魅力。它借鉴了巴厘人几乎各个层面的经验，汇集了主题——动物野蛮、男性自恋、对手赌博、地位竞争、大众兴奋、血祭——其主要联系是他们对愤怒的参与和对愤怒的恐惧，并将它们绑定到一套既包含它们又允许它们玩耍的规则中，构建了一个象征性结构，在这个象征性结构中，人们可以一遍又一遍地清晰地感受到他们内心归属的现实。如果，再次引用诺斯罗普·弗莱的话，如果我们去看麦克白，了解一个人在获得王国并失去灵魂后的感受，巴厘人去斗鸡，了解一个通常沉着、冷漠、几乎痴迷于自我中心的人，一种道德自体，在受到攻击、折磨、挑战、侮辱，最终被逼到极端愤怒时，他的感觉是怎样的，他完全胜利了，还是完全被彻底征服了。低。
